originalTitle: Canara Robeco Asset Management shares rally 13% after Q1FY27 profit jumps 24% YoY
simplifiedContent: Canara Robeco Asset Management's stock price increased by 13% after the company reported a good start to the financial year. The company's profit increased by 24% compared to the same time last year, which made investors happy and confident. The company's revenue from its main business also grew by 20% to ₹116.2 crore, which is a good sign. This growth in revenue and profit is why the company's stock price went up, as investors are more likely to buy the stock when they see the company doing well. This matters because it shows that the company is performing well and may continue to do so, which could be good for investors who own the stock.

originalTitle: Cube Highways Trust InvIT raises Rs 1,687 crore from Premji Invest, other anchor investors ahead of its IPO
simplifiedContent: Here's a simplified version of the news: Cube Highways Trust InvIT, a company that invests in roads, has received Rs 1,687.5 crore from some big investors before its initial public offering (IPO) starts on July 22. This IPO is expected to raise a total of Rs 5,000 crore. The company is selling existing shares, and investing in it will give people a chance to own a part of many roads across India. This is a notable development because it shows that big investors are interested in the company, which could be a good sign for others who are thinking of investing.

originalTitle: Anant Raj demerger: Data centre arm to spin out as separate listed company, what lies ahead for 4 lakh shareholders
simplifiedContent: Anant Raj, a company, is splitting off its data centre and cloud businesses into a new, separate company called Ashok Cloud. This means that Ashok Cloud will become its own listed company, allowing investors to buy and sell its shares directly. As a result, shareholders of Anant Raj will receive shares of Ashok Cloud, with every Anant Raj share entitling them to two Ashok Cloud shares. This change is subject to approval from regulators and a specific date will be announced to determine which shareholders are eligible. This matters because it gives Anant Raj's 400,000 shareholders a chance to own a part of the growing digital infrastructure business directly.

originalTitle: CJP protest in Delhi Jantar Mantar: Why India can't afford this crisis to last long amid US-Iran war? Explained
simplifiedContent: There are protests happening in Delhi, and experts are worried that if they go on for too long, it could hurt India's economy. This is because foreign investors might lose confidence in the country and decide not to put their money in. Political stability and clear policies are important for investors to feel safe and want to invest. If India can't show stability, it could scare away investors, which would be bad for the country's economy. This is especially concerning right now because of the tensions between the US and Iran, which is already making the global economy uncertain.

originalTitle: Cube Highways Trust InvIT IPO opens today; check latest GMP, subscription status, review, key details
simplifiedContent: Cube Highways Trust is selling shares to the public for the first time through an initial public offering (IPO) that starts today and ends on July 24. The price of each share will be between ₹151 and ₹152. Before the IPO, the company already raised ₹1,687.5 crore from big investors like mutual funds. This is important because it shows that these major investors are interested in the company, which might affect how the public offering goes. The IPO's success could depend on how much interest it gets from regular investors like you.

originalTitle: Expert view: Nifty's core growth drivers remain attractive, valuation offers margin of safety, says Bharti AXA Life CIO
simplifiedContent: The Chief Investment Officer (CIO) of Bharti AXA Life thinks that the Indian stock market, also known as the Nifty, is still a good place to invest because its main drivers of growth are strong. The CIO also likes that the current prices of stocks are reasonable, which makes it a relatively safe time to invest. This is despite there being some big global issues that could affect the market. The expert suggests spreading investments across different areas to reduce risk. The CIO believes that investments from foreign countries could help the market grow even more in the future.
